model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Houchin: a Republican-leaning district, incumbency, and an overwhelming fundraising edge over Brad Meyer, who has raised only about $105K. Prediction markets agree, pricing her win probability near 94%, so the forecast stays close to the fundamentals-based margin with modest widening for her money advantage.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Meyer competitive, or significant outside spending entering the district, would be the first sign the race is closer than expected.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Erin Houchin, the Republican incumbent, is seeking another term in a southern Indiana district that leans heavily Republican, with a partisan baseline of about R+15. Democrat Brad Meyer has raised roughly $105K and ends with under $20K on hand, while Houchin has raised about $1.9M and holds more than $1.1M in cash. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but has raised almost nothing.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which give Houchin about a 94% chance of winning. Everything points to a comfortable Republican hold, with only a small chance of an upset if the national environment shifts sharply.
